## 固定收益主線

10月22日，全球科技股下挫，法國公債壓力加深，避險買盤湧入美債，其力道壓過油價再度急漲帶來的通膨壓力。10年期美債殖利率下跌16.6個基點至4.953%，約一個月來首次跌破5%。2年期殖利率降幅幾乎相同；交易員將市場完全反映聯準會再度升息的時點，由12月延後至1月。

這波買盤不只是在防範股價下跌。投資人開始重估，人工智慧投資的成本與規模，會不會反過來傷害原先支撐緊縮政策預期的經濟成長。Meta龐大的未來支出承諾，以及單季轉負的自由現金流，使疑慮更加具體，也將其違約保障成本推至新高。美債期貨空頭回補加速公債漲勢，美國高收益債與強勢貨幣計價新興市場債券利差則明顯擴大。

資金搶進核心公債之際，法國卻逆勢遭到拋售。法國相對德國的殖利率溢價盤中達178個基點，財政與政治前景未明，又遇上流動性不佳及新一輪利差收益部位平倉，連短天期法債也下跌。其他央行面對的抉擇同樣分歧：菲律賓意外升息半個百分點，南韓暫停升息但上調成長評估，土耳其則在通膨放緩後降息。美債大漲反映的是市場大幅重估成長與金融情勢，全球通膨問題並未因此消退。

## 美債買盤由長端擴及短中天期

對政策敏感的短中天期美債與長債一同上漲。2年期殖利率下降16.64個基點至4.6396%，5年期下降17.93個基點至4.7713%；30年期降幅較小，為12.85個基點，收在5.2804%。2年期與10年期降幅幾乎相同，使2年／10年期利差僅擴大0.04個基點至31.34個基點，大致持平；短端表現優於30年期，2年／30年期利差擴大3.79個基點至64.08個基點。

週四的買盤因而有別於只推升長天期債券的行情。Bloomberg形容，這是美債一年多來最強的漲勢，部分天期殖利率盤中一度下降達20個基點。BMO Capital Markets的Ian Lyngen指出，科技股修正促使投資人思考：市場本身造成的金融情勢緊縮，是否足以讓貨幣政策不必維持那麼高的限制程度。貨幣市場不再完全反映聯準會年底前升息，但1月升息25個基點仍已完全反映在價格中。

這次名目殖利率下降，主要來自實質借款成本降低。10年期抗通膨債券實質殖利率下降13.77個基點至2.6117%，相對應的損益兩平通膨率則下降2.83個基點至2.3413%。通膨補償下降也有助於名目公債上漲，但實質殖利率的調整大得多，顯示公債需求與成長疑慮已成為強大力量。

若拉長比較期間，10年期殖利率一週下降10.5個基點，但仍比一個月前高0.1個基點；30年期一週下降12.52個基點，一個月僅下降0.46個基點。2年期的一週與一個月降幅則分別為9.86與10.84個基點。週四行情明顯舒緩了最近一輪殖利率上升的壓力，但長期融資成本仍接近一個月前。

既有空頭部位放大了走勢。Bloomberg報導，投資人解除看空部位，美債期貨出現一波買盤。CME週三未平倉資料顯示，長債期貨風險部位大幅增加；報導將其辨識為新建空頭，因此在週四債價上漲時容易受到擠壓。價格愈漲，這些既有部位愈需要買進回補。

選擇權市場也出現防範美債繼續上漲的需求。對沖進一步漲勢所需的權利金升至3月以來最高；較長天期美債選擇權的一項指標顯示，買權相對賣權出現七個月來首次溢價。週四上午累積的一筆部位，押注10年期殖利率一個月內朝4.6%下降，規模約6.5萬口，權利金約$700萬。

油價則構成顯著的反向壓力。布蘭特原油期貨收在每桶$112.80，單日上漲3.66%，一週上漲6.50%，一個月上漲17.21%；WTI上漲1.90%至$99。美國下令非緊急政府人員及家屬撤離沙烏地阿拉伯，區域安全疑慮升高。沙烏地阿美的Shaybah油田遭無人機攻擊，造成兩人死亡，但營運未中斷；另一起針對法赫德國王國際機場的攻擊也造成傷亡。據報，沙烏地阿美並已疏散達蘭總部，要求員工居家工作。

債券上漲之時，能源衝擊仍在持續，只是眼前的影響已不局限於通膨：昂貴燃料也威脅家庭與企業支出。Invesco Fixed Income的Robert Waldner表示，公司一直在等待殖利率上升開始造成損害的跡象，而AI疑慮使他認為殖利率暫時已見頂。TJM Institutional Services策略師David Robin也指出，這次出現了新的成長擔憂，不能只當成單純轉向高品質資產的避險行情。

最新美國數據對當前景氣的描述仍有分歧。截至10月17日當週，初領失業救濟金人數降至19.4萬人，低於市場預期20萬人，也低於前期修正後的20萬人。截至10月10日當週，續領人數卻增至172.8萬人，高於預期172.0萬人及前期修正後的170.3萬人。新增申請減少，但持續領取者增加，兩項指標方向不同，尚未呈現勞動市場突然轉弱的一致訊號。

9月世界大型企業研究會領先指標月增率為零，優於預期下降0.1%，前期亦下降0.1%。地區製造業數據則放緩：堪薩斯聯準銀行10月綜合指數由14降至11，符合預測；另一項製造業指數由20降至16，低於預測18。整體成長表現更不均衡，製造業趨緩，但初領失業救濟金與領先指標的主要讀值都優於預期。

房貸成本小幅回落，每週30年期房貸利率由7.4%降至7.32%，15年期由6.71%降至6.68%。總統川普週四簽署行政命令，要求聯邦住宅金融局（FHFA）設立試辦計畫，針對部分未來承作的貸款，在房價增值足以支持取消保險時，主動取消房貸保險。命令也要求農業部與退伍軍人事務部調降其承作的獨戶住宅房貸利率，並成立工作小組處理預製住宅成本。

該命令另將產權保險試辦計畫永久化，讓部分再融資交易可以自動化產權審查，取代保障貸款人的產權保險。FHFA局長Bill Pulte另外表示，正研究減少使用信用報告的份數，以及可能調整貸款層級定價加減碼，後者預計年底前決定。房貸利率仍高於7%，這些措施著眼於貸款承作與保險費用，作用範圍有別於市場利率全面下降。

美國財政部亦完成$260億5年期抗通膨債券（TIPS）標售，實質得標殖利率為2.367%，是該天期2023年10月以來最高。據Bloomberg，得標殖利率比截標時市場殖利率高出不到1個基點。即使次級市場全面上漲，投資人仍在標售中取得略為便宜的進場價格。

跨資產跌勢主要集中在科技與其他風險敏感資產。Nasdaq 100下跌2.88%，半導體股下跌6.71%，標普500下跌1.21%；VIX上升14.09%至19.03。黃金期貨下跌2.59%，收每盎司$4,042.40，美元指數小跌0.07%。能源價格持續上漲之際，公債仍是防禦性資金流入最明顯的資產。

## Meta支出承諾使AI融資風險浮現

Meta信用狀況惡化，讓科技股跌勢背後的融資疑慮有了具體依據。據ICE Data Services，其5年期信用違約交換（CDS）報價一度上升8.9個基點至每年約119.3個基點，創約一年前開始活躍交易以來的盤中新高。票息5.25%、2036年到期債券的對美債利差擴大7個基點至121個基點。Oracle、Microsoft與Broadcom的違約保障成本也上升。

Meta新揭露的未來租賃與契約承諾約$8,250億，高於7月公布的近$7,000億，其中許多涉及運算能力及AI基礎設施。同季自由現金流轉為負$21.2億，相較之下，第2季為流入$7.84億，去年第3季則流入$106.25億。未來義務增加之際，這組現金流比較也讓債權人面臨更嚴峻的評估。

公司先前已將全年資本支出區間下限由$1,300億提高至$1,350億，上限維持$1,450億，且未提供明年資本支出指引。週四的信用市場反應，是將這項已知的支出調整，與更龐大的契約承諾及現金流出放在一起考量。投資人普遍預期，Meta會在財報公布後、下次聯準會會議及11月3日選舉之前再度發債，也因此更加關注既有債券利差。

雲端最佳化公司DoiT International執行長Vadim Solovey指出，Meta的承諾期間很長，資料中心租約可達18至30年。他認為，在容量稀缺之際簽下這類協議成本高昂，但Meta既有業務同樣會使用這些運算資源，因此比許多其他買家更具優勢。對一個現在就希望從AI取得營運回報、卻把現金承諾延伸到多年以後的借款人，這項區別相當重要。

Morgan Stanley的Vishwanath Tirupattur認為，即使借款成本再上升100個基點，也不太可能阻止超大規模雲端業者投入資本支出；但影響不會平均分布，生態系較下游、體質較弱的借款人會更脆弱。他判斷，今年大部分利差擴大，是市場消化大量新債供給的結果。因此，即使資本支出放緩削弱股市的成長敘事，只要能減少債券供給，信用市場反而可能正面看待。

市場對需求仍有重大分歧。Blackstone總裁Jon Gray表示，AI基礎設施的興建是為了跟上現有需求，反駁Ken Griffin幾天前提出的泡沫疑慮。BlackRock的Wei Li則強調，殖利率上升使仰賴遠期成長的投資面臨更高報酬要求，投資人愈來愈要求看到AI變現。相較於Meta對自身投資回報的信心，Tesla決定削減支出計畫，以及晶片設備商Lam Research低於預期的展望，提供了不同的營運訊號。

中國市場進一步顯示風險偏好惡化。滬深300收跌1.8%，較6月高點累計下跌20%；中國境內股市自近期高點已蒸發$2.4兆市值，恒生科技指數週四也下跌約5%。消費疲弱、AI獲利前景受質疑，加上未見大規模支出方案的失望情緒，共同壓抑市場。當地時間下午2時45分，九檔與國家資金買盤相關的ETF成交額達人民幣520億元，接近10月15日的人民幣628億元，當局試圖緩和賣壓。

即使公開市場下跌，大額新融資仍然可行。知情人士表示，DeepSeek完成約$150億募資，寧德時代與騰訊為最大投資人之列；另一名知情人士表示，華為取得中資銀行$22.5億貸款。公開市場投資人質疑估值與未來回報之際，這些企業仍獲得可觀的新資本。

澳洲的AI建設則面臨實體條件限制。Bloomberg報導，雪梨與墨爾本周邊逾40個規劃中或興建中的大型資料中心計畫，僅23%已公開確認電力供應或電網連接。澳洲已宣布及早期規劃案的容量超過20GW，現有營運容量約1.5GW。資料中心目前已占電網用電約2%，預計2036年增至13%。Goodman的一項雪梨計畫在收到數百項反對意見後取消，規模為A$12億。

這些限制凸顯，為已宣布的容量融資，與為真正能產生收入的容量融資，是不同的事。電網接入與地方核准決定建物何時可投入使用，借款與施工承諾卻可能早已開始。這個產業仍吸引大量新資金，但融資評估正變得更有選擇性。

週四整體信用市場同時反映公債上漲與風險溢酬增加。美國高收益債及強勢貨幣計價新興市場債券利差明顯擴大；投資級債券ETF LQD報酬約1.03%，高收益債基金HYG為0.18%，新興市場債券基金EMB為0.45%。美債殖利率下降支撐債券正報酬，但較脆弱借款人面對的信用條件已惡化。

## 法債遭拋售，與歐洲核心公債分歧

投資人願意持有美國與德國主權債，卻繼續拋售法國風險，法債再度明顯惡化。10年期法債相對德國公債的溢價一度擴大19個基點至178個基點，是2011年底以來最大差距。法國10年期殖利率盤中最高上升13個基點至5.14%，創2002年以來最高，之後在報導涵蓋的交易時段內收斂至上升約6個基點。

賣壓也延伸到短端，2年期殖利率上升11個基點至3.86%，CAC 40跌逾1%。據Bloomberg美國交易時段後段的報導，德國10年期殖利率下降9個基點至3.33%，英國下降5個基點至5.33%。法債遭到拋售，其他公債卻獲得買盤，進一步拉大了法國的殖利率溢價。

Mediolanum International Funds的Daniel Loughney表示，新一輪利差收益部位平倉又遭流動性不佳放大。這些部位原先試圖賺取短天期法債與利率交換間的利差；如今解除部位，為市場增添賣壓。民眾抗議生活成本高漲，政府能否修復公共財政仍不明朗，法債原已承受壓力。

總統馬克宏表示，政府將以週六只允許工會遊行為目標。警方禁止巴黎部分地區示威，包括總統府附近與香榭麗舍大道沿線，其他城市也實施限制。週末可能再起動盪，使投資人必須同時評估財政協商，以及政府抑制干擾的能力。

Aegon Investment Management的Irina Kurochkina將疲弱情緒歸因於能源價格、流動性薄弱與預算不確定性。她認為，若ECB承認殖利率上升已使金融情勢驟然收緊，從而降低進一步升息的急迫性，便能支持債券。Allspring的Henrietta Pacquement則認為，短期內恢復信心的催化因素不多；明年的總統大選也使殖利率約5%的吸引力更難評估。

ECB管理委員會委員Fabio Panetta從經濟承受的壓力提出另一種觀點。他週三在杜林表示，殖利率上升將拖累歐洲經濟，但還未構成危機。這波升勢由美國帶動，美國經濟成長較強、利率也較高，歐洲卻是在活動相對疲弱的情況下承受融資緊縮。他也警告，法國主權債緊張可能影響義大利借款成本。

Guinness Global Investors的Craig Veysey強調，歐洲安全網比過去更強，也未出現先前債務危機時的銀行壓力。他擔心，若情勢更廣泛惡化，投資人開始預期德國須增加借款、支援負債沉重的鄰國，壓力最終可能波及德國。週四德債仍在上漲。

歐洲決策者另就證券化規則改革達成暫時政治協議，試圖透過另一途徑擴大信用供給。架構將大幅降低低風險交易的銀行資本要求，對風險較高的部位仍保留較高要求，目前尚待定案與正式認可。

折衷方案在既有「簡單、透明及標準化」（STS）標籤之外，新增「具韌性」類別，將獨立STS驗證機構納入歐盟層級監管，並減少行政要求；也將提高UCITS基金投資上限，允許保險與再保險業者更廣泛參與合成型證券化，包括為尚未開始營運的計畫提供融資的交易。據歐洲金融市場協會，3月底歐洲證券化未償餘額含擔保貸款憑證（CLO）共€1.295兆，年增6.3%。

改革希望釋出銀行資本，供家庭、企業及基礎設施放貸，包括國防與氣候韌性投資。法債遭拋售顯示主權融資條件能迅速收緊，這套方案則著眼於信用中介的能力與成本；其效益取決於架構能否完成，以及修訂後的規則能否吸引投資人參與。

## 各國政策顯現不同通膨制約

菲律賓是當天最鮮明的意外緊縮案例，將目標逆回購利率提高50個基點至5.50%。Bloomberg調查的25名經濟學家中，僅一人預期這個幅度，其餘24人均預期25個基點。總裁Eli Remolona表示，通膨前景比預期更差，必須急切因應，央行也表明準備好再次行動。

菲律賓央行維持2026年通膨預測6.1%，卻將2027年預測由5.4%上調至6%，預計要到2028年才會降至3.3%。9月通膨加速至7.2%，扭轉連續四個月放緩的趨勢，年初至今平均為5.4%，高於3%目標。油價上漲、交通費調高，加上聖嬰現象可能帶來嚴重乾旱，讓本已處於疫情以來最慢成長速度的經濟更加難以應對。

即使升息，披索仍再創新低。Remolona承認進口通膨壓力，但表示不會為捍衛特定匯率而耗盡外匯存底。自伊朗戰爭開始以來，累計升息已達125個基點。Pantheon Macroeconomics的Miguel Chanco認為，這次較大幅度的升息，可能已將原本12月才會進行的升息提前。

南韓則一致決議，將7天期附買回利率維持3%，符合全部24名受訪經濟學家的預期；此前7月與8月各升息25個基點。暫停升息同時，南韓央行提高對成長的評估，表示今明兩年將明顯超過8月預測的3.3%與2.9%。總裁申鉉松表示，先前升息已創造空間，可以評估國內情勢，不必機械式回應短期市場變化。

央行亦預期，明年核心通膨將略高於先前預測的2.5%，11月將公布更新預測；先前整體通膨預測為2026年2.7%、2027年2.3%。申鉉松接受通膨以較漸進方式接近目標，不要求明年立即回到目標。State Street的Jiuk Choi預期，至少還會升息一次，之後長時間維持利率不變，等待核心通膨在2027年底前放緩至2%區間的低端至中段。

國內細節說明了為何政策步調謹慎。10月前20天，經工作日調整的出口年增65.9%，晶片出口大增222.5%；但9月銀行家庭放款僅增加6,000億韓元，是3月以來最小增幅，房貸成長放緩。截至10月19日當週，首爾公寓價格仍上漲0.13%，連漲89週。週四稍早，3年期公債殖利率一度上升3個基點，韓元一度升值0.3%至每美元1,322.75韓元。

土耳其走向寬鬆，將一週附買回利率由37%下調至36%，為伊朗戰爭開始以來首次降息，隔夜放款與借款利率也分別降至39%與34.5%。9月年通膨率降至29.7%，為2021年11月以來最低，需求與經濟活動亦趨緩。總裁Fatih Karahan領導的委員會仍採逐次會議決策，重點放在通膨前景。

降息前，國內投資基金也經歷嚴重壓力。監管機關下令清算131檔基金，總值約$200億。財政部長Mehmet Simsek本週表示，近50萬名受影響投資人中，僅不到5萬人收到款項，合計408億里拉。央行已增加附買回融資，並放寬部分小企業信用成長限制，以緩解流動性壓力。Is Asset Management的Hande Sekerci預期，負財富效果將削弱消費，為進一步寬鬆創造空間，同時也理解央行對10月通膨波動保持謹慎。

墨西哥最新通膨數據則使政策選擇更棘手。10月上半月消費者物價年增率加速至3.62%，高於市場預期3.59%及9月下半月的3.49%；核心通膨升至3.78%，同樣高於預測3.70%與前值3.71%。墨西哥央行自6月起將基準利率維持6.5%，最近將偏向持續按兵不動的指引，改為更依數據決策。新數據增加11月5日決策前的壓力，央行仍預測通膨將於2027年第4季收斂至3%目標。

捷克央行副總裁Jan Frait對能源通膨的回應更保留。他表示，11月5日再度升息的理由相對充分，但市場利率已在抑制經濟活動。對房貸定價重要的3年期利率交換，自伊朗戰爭開始以來已上升約150個基點至接近4.9%。核心通膨為3.1%，新增房貸活動開始出現放緩跡象，企業信用則仍強勁。

Frait不認為目前情況需要未來一年升息100個基點，並質疑市場定價是否部分反映流動性或機械式模型。即使經濟保持韌性、全球通膨壓力持續，他也認為升息50個基點顯得急驟。若放款未放緩、需求仍強且加薪要求增加，他才會回應。他區分的是：因應持續的國內壓力，與在較長天期市場利率已造成的緊縮之上再加碼。

日本長端吸引的買盤性質不同。BNP Paribas Asset Management的James McAlevey表示，公司將20年與30年期日本公債部位，由年初很小的規模增至中等或適中水準；部分彈性策略同時放空2年與5年期債券。他看重陡峭的殖利率曲線、約6%至6.5%的美元避險後殖利率，以及國內需求回升，日本保險業者已連續四個月淨買進超長天期公債。進一步增強信心，仍有賴財政行動受約束、BOJ持續大致每季推進政策正常化，並由較強日圓協助壓抑進口通膨。

## 個別信用惡化，融資交易仍在進行

JetBlue下週公布財報前，旗下證券再度重挫。其$20億、2031年到期、以常客計畫支持的債券，由10月初每1美元面額約80美分跌至約40美分，創歷史新低。股價跌近10%至$2.65，為2002年上市以來最低。高燃油成本打擊這家本已負債沉重、連年虧損，且休閒旅客對價格敏感的航空公司。

公司重申對轉型有信心，目標仍是2028年每股盈餘至少$1；先前並預測2027年自由現金流轉正，且揭露逾$60億未設定擔保的資產。不過，第2季自由現金流為負$3.89億，其中營運消耗$1.55億，資本支出$2.34億。每加侖平均燃油成本$4.23，年增76%。Moody's給予Caa2評等，並預估今明兩年虧損，構成公司試圖安撫債權人的背景。

知情人士表示，土耳其電力公司Zorlu Enerji正準備就$11億債券週五到期的約$5,500萬利息，尋求最多延後六個月支付。其2030年到期債券週四報價約每1美元面額50多美分的中段。Fitch於9月將其降評至B-並列負向觀察，理由是流動性轉弱、依賴短期再融資。Fitch指出，截至6月，未來12個月有$1.245億債務到期，預期2026與2027年自由現金流為負，今年利息成本將消耗約65%的現金EBITDA。

EyeCare Partners則接近與債權人達成附條件協議，以出售資產減債。Anchorage Capital、Diameter與King Street等貸款人同意，若業務在約定期限內售出，可接受債權折價；出售較慢，折價幅度便縮小，未能出售則不再給予折價。據熟悉條款的人士，最有利情境可從約$20億債務中減少$3億至$4億。

其中，驗光業務出售給MyEyeDr的交易，預計在取得監管核准後於第4季完成。所得將按面額償還$1.10億第一順位受償循環額度，以及$2.86億第一順位受償定期貸款。S&P表示，約$1.64億第一留置權、第二順位受償債務，將以每1美元面額折讓12美分償還。參與困境換債的第二順位貸款人，將轉入新的第一留置權1.5順位受償貸款，並可選擇將以債付息（PIK）期間延至2027年初之後、到期日延至2028年11月之後。對不同債權人而言，協議價值取決於債權順位與時間安排，不只是減債總額。

其他交易顯示，企業仍能取得私人融資。Blackstone主導$3億融資組合，支援Arlington Capital Partners將航太與國防零組件製造商Gooch & Housego下市收購；Arlington最初以股權資金完成收購。融資包括單一級別貸款（unitranche）、延遲動用定期貸款與循環額度，JPMorgan及Jefferies也參與。

知情人士表示，德州開發商KDC正尋求約$35億，以信用租戶租約融資興建AT&T位於普萊諾的新總部。CGA Capital與CBRE安排的債務，預期加權平均年限為18.7年。這種結構仰賴投資級租戶支付的租金，而非底層不動產本身；擬議規模也遠高於PGIM所稱此類交易常見的$2,500萬至$1億。

Blackstone自身財報反映營運環境不均。交易活動放緩，可分配盈餘下降9.2%至$17.2億，每股$1.32，仍優於市場預期$1.26。信用與保險業務盈餘增加4%至$4.33億，且占單季$633億資金流入的一半以上。基礎設施報酬6.4%，部分受資料中心租賃支持；不動產與私募股權可分配盈餘則分別下降10%與7%。儘管可用資本有$2,289億，單季投入的$301億仍是今年各季最低。

主權借款人也尋求替代資金來源。印尼在上海與投資人會面，規劃11月至12月初可能發行人民幣70億至100億元熊貓債，天期可能涵蓋3年、5年與7年；已獲准在2028年前發行最多人民幣300億元。融資官員Suminto表示，7月首次發行人民幣70億元後，較低成本與擴大投資人基礎，是再度進場的理由。不過，與MSCI相關的資金外流風險，仍使其金融環境更為複雜。

南非財政部指出，國家預算之下還有地方融資弱點：截至6月的一年，市政機關對債權人的債務增加19%至1,852億蘭特；截至8月31日，光是對Eskom的逾期欠款已達1,225億蘭特。Eskom先前已取得2,300億蘭特紓困方案中的2,200億蘭特，財政部仍警告，陷入困境的公共實體可能需要更多中央資金或擔保。擬議市政財政改革將要求個人對違規支出負責，允許財政部任命市政財務長，並要求議會就缺乏財源支持的預算提出交代。

奈及利亞財政部長Taiwo Oyedele預期，收入改善及借款成本下降，將使聯邦赤字低於GDP的4.2%目標；世界銀行涵蓋州與地方政府的較廣義合併預測，卻顯示赤字將擴大。另有比較指出，上半年利息支出比聯邦收入高24%，財政部對此提出異議，表示利息數字納入代其他層級政府支付的債務義務，收入數字卻漏列部分收入。截至6月，總公共債務年增21%至$1,210億。

## 後續市場焦點

週五公布的10月S&P Global PMI初值，將接在一波已擴及短中天期、並降低近期聯準會升息預期的美債漲勢之後。數據於UTC 13:45發布，製造業共識為55.5，前值55.9；服務業預期58，前值58.8；綜合指數預測為57.6，前值58.4。投資人愈來愈在意昂貴資本對成長的代價，PMI將為週四偏低的初領失業救濟金與轉弱的地區製造業數據，提供更廣泛的景氣對照。

10月密西根大學調查終值於UTC 14:00公布。消費者信心預期46.3，前值48.1；現況指數預期44.7，前值50.9。一年與五年通膨預期分別估4.7%及3.5%，前值為4.6%及3.4%。若信心轉弱，通膨預期卻居高不下，聯準會面對的組合將不同於經濟放緩且物價預期同步下降。週四實質殖利率大降之後，這項差異對漲勢能否延續更具影響。

週一則有9月芝加哥聯準銀行全國活動指數，預測-0.1，前值-0.04；10月達拉斯聯準銀行製造業指數預測7，前值9.8，另有2年期美債標售。景氣數據將擴大成長評估的範圍，標售則可觀察短債殖利率大幅重定價後，投資人的實際承接需求。

AI融資是企業端眼前的考驗。Meta承諾增加且現金流出，任何新借款的條件與規模都很重要；下週Alphabet、Microsoft與Amazon財報，則將分別更新支出與轉化為收入的進度。JetBlue在擔保債券跌近每1美元面額40美分之際公布財報，流動性與創造現金的能力尤其迫切。Zorlu Enerji週五的付息期限，將決定擬議展延的下一步。

法國歷經利差衝擊與利差收益部位平倉，週末示威及政府回應仍對市場有直接意義。被迫賣出已延伸至短天期，因此除了財政進展，流動性能否改善也很重要。能源風險則獨立持續，攻擊威脅沙烏地基礎設施，即使部分設施營運仍正常。燃料成本若再上升，可能同時加重家庭需求與通膨的壓力；菲律賓上修通膨預測，正顯示這種組合能持續制約貨幣政策。

overall_summary.headline: 科技股重挫、法債壓力加深成長疑慮，美債大漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
全球科技股下挫與法國主權債壓力，帶動避險需求，也促使投資人重估成長，美債各天期全面上漲。10年期殖利率下降16.6個基點至4.953%，約一個月來首次低於5%；2年期下降16.64個基點至4.6396%。交易員將下一次完全反映在價格中的聯準會升息，由12月延後至1月，美債期貨空頭回補進一步放大漲勢。10年期實質殖利率下降13.77個基點，是主要推力，損益兩平通膨率則小幅下降2.83個基點。

Meta約$8,250億未來租賃與契約承諾，以及單季負$21.2億的自由現金流，使AI投資回報疑慮升高。其違約保障成本創盤中新高，美國高收益債及強勢貨幣計價新興市場債券利差也明顯擴大。法國與核心公債漲勢分歧：財政不確定、流動性薄弱與利差收益部位平倉，使賣壓延伸至短天期，對德國的殖利率溢價盤中達178個基點。

沙烏地基礎設施遭攻擊，油價持續上漲，高能源成本仍威脅支出與通膨。菲律賓意外升息50個基點，南韓維持利率但提高成長評估，土耳其則因通膨放緩而降息。週五美國景氣與通膨預期數據，有助辨別眼前是經濟成長放緩，還是需求轉弱、物價壓力卻持續的更棘手組合。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries surged on October 22 as a global technology selloff and deepening stress in French government debt drove investors toward safety, overwhelming the inflation pressure from another sharp rise in oil. The 10-year yield fell 16.6 basis points to 4.953%, dropping below 5% for the first time in about a month. Two-year yields declined almost as much as traders pushed back the point at which another Federal Reserve increase was fully priced from December to January.

The change extended beyond a demand for protection against falling share prices. Investors were reassessing whether the cost and scale of artificial-intelligence investment could undermine the growth that had helped sustain expectations of tighter policy. Meta's future spending commitments and negative quarterly free cash flow sharpened that concern, sending its default-protection costs to a new high. Treasury futures short covering accelerated the government-bond advance, while U.S. high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably.

France moved in the opposite direction from the rush into core government debt. Its premium over Germany reached 178 basis points during trading, and even short-dated French bonds sold off as poor liquidity and renewed carry-position liquidations compounded fiscal and political uncertainty. Elsewhere, central banks faced markedly different choices: the Philippines delivered a surprise half-point increase, South Korea paused while strengthening its growth assessment, and Turkey cut rates as inflation slowed. The U.S. rally was a substantial reassessment of growth and financial conditions, rather than evidence that the global inflation problem had passed.

## Treasury Buying Broadens Beyond the Long End

The rally reached the policy-sensitive part of the Treasury curve as well as longer maturities. Two-year yields fell 16.64 basis points to 4.6396%, and five-year yields declined 17.93 basis points to 4.7713%. The 30-year yield fell a smaller 12.85 basis points to 5.2804%. With the two- and 10-year moves almost identical, the 2s10s spread was effectively steady at 31.34 basis points, widening just 0.04 basis point. The 2s30s spread increased 3.79 basis points to 64.08 as the front end outperformed the long bond.

That breadth distinguished Thursday's buying from a rally confined to distant cash flows. Bloomberg described the Treasury advance as the strongest in more than a year, with yields falling as much as 20 basis points at some maturities during the session. BMO Capital Markets' Ian Lyngen said the technology correction had prompted investors to consider whether market-driven tightening of financial conditions could warrant a less restrictive monetary-policy path. Money markets ceased fully pricing a Fed increase by year-end, although a quarter-point rise remained fully priced for January.

The move was principally a decline in real borrowing costs. The 10-year inflation-linked yield fell 13.77 basis points to 2.6117%, while the corresponding breakeven declined 2.83 basis points to 2.3413%. Lower inflation compensation contributed to the nominal rally, but the much larger real-yield adjustment showed how strongly demand for government debt and concerns about growth had taken hold.

The longer comparisons put the size of the daily move in perspective. Ten-year yields were down 10.5 basis points over the week but still 0.1 basis point above their level a month earlier. The 30-year was 12.52 basis points lower over the week and only 0.46 basis point lower over the month. At two years, the declines were 9.86 and 10.84 basis points, respectively. Thursday delivered considerable relief from the latest rise in yields without leaving long-term financing costs far below their month-earlier levels.

Short positioning helped magnify the change. Bloomberg reported a wave of buying in Treasury futures as investors unwound bearish positions. CME open-interest figures from Wednesday had shown a substantial build-up of long-bond futures risk, which the reporting identified as fresh short positions vulnerable to Thursday's advance. The reversal thus encountered investors whose existing exposure required buying as prices rose.

Options trading showed a parallel demand for protection against a further rally. The premium for hedging additional Treasury gains rose to its highest since March. In longer-dated Treasury options, one measure put calls at a premium to puts for the first time in seven months. A position accumulated during Thursday morning targeted a decline in the 10-year yield toward 4.6% within a month, reaching roughly 65,000 contracts at a premium of about $7 million. That was the payoff sought by the trade, not a consensus yield forecast.

Oil supplied a substantial opposing pressure. Brent futures finished at $112.80 a barrel, up 3.66% on the day, 6.50% over the week and 17.21% over the month. WTI rose 1.90% to $99. The U.S. order for non-emergency government personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia intensified concern about regional security. A drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field killed two people without interrupting operations, while a separate attack on King Fahd International Airport caused casualties. Aramco was also reported to have evacuated its Dhahran headquarters and instructed employees to work from home.

The energy shock was therefore still active while bonds rallied. Its immediate market significance had broadened: expensive fuel threatened household and corporate spending as well as inflation. Invesco Fixed Income's Robert Waldner said the firm had been waiting for evidence that the rise in yields was beginning to cause damage, and regarded the AI concerns as a reason to think yields had peaked for now. TJM Institutional Services strategist David Robin distinguished the new concern about growth from a straightforward flight to quality.

Fresh U.S. releases nevertheless gave a mixed account of current activity. Initial unemployment claims fell to 194,000 in the week ended October 17, below both the 200,000 consensus and the revised previous reading of 200,000. Continuing claims increased to 1.728 million for the week ended October 10, exceeding the 1.720 million consensus and a revised 1.703 million previously. Fewer new benefit applications sat alongside a larger number continuing to receive benefits, leaving the two measures pointing in different directions rather than establishing a sudden labor-market break.

September's Conference Board leading index was unchanged on the month, stronger than the expected 0.1% decline and the previous 0.1% fall. Regional manufacturing readings softened: the Kansas Fed composite index slipped to 11 in October from 14, matching the calendar forecast, while the separately titled manufacturing index declined to 16 from 20, below a forecast of 18. These observations supported a more uneven growth picture, with moderation in manufacturing but firmer-than-expected claims and leading-index headlines.

Mortgage costs eased modestly. The weekly 30-year mortgage rate was 7.32%, down from 7.4%, while the 15-year rate declined to 6.68% from 6.71%. President Donald Trump signed an executive order Thursday directing the Federal Housing Finance Agency to establish a pilot that would proactively cancel mortgage insurance on certain future loans when home appreciation justified it. The order also directs the Agriculture and Veterans Affairs departments to lower rates on the single-family mortgages they make and establishes a task force on manufactured-housing costs.

The directive makes a title-insurance pilot permanent, allowing automated title review to replace a lender's title policy on certain refinancing transactions. Separately, FHFA Director Bill Pulte said the agency was studying the use of fewer credit reports and potential changes to loan-level pricing adjustments, with a decision on the latter anticipated before year-end. The measures address origination and insurance expenses while mortgage rates remain above 7%; their scope differs from a general reduction in market interest rates.

Treasury also completed its $26 billion five-year TIPS auction at a real yield of 2.367%, the highest for the tenor since October 2023. The award was less than 1 basis point above the prevailing yield at the bidding deadline, according to Bloomberg. It provided a modestly cheaper entry at auction even during the broad secondary-market rally.

Across assets, the retreat was concentrated in technology and other risk-sensitive holdings. The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.88%, semiconductor shares dropped 6.71%, and the S&P 500 lost 1.21%. The VIX rose 14.09% to 19.03. Gold futures declined 2.59% to $4,042.40 an ounce, while the Dollar Index edged down 0.07%. Government debt attracted the strongest defensive response despite the continuing rise in energy prices.

## Meta's Commitments Bring AI Funding Into Focus

Meta's credit deterioration supplied a concrete financing development behind the technology retreat. Five-year credit-default swaps rose as much as 8.9 basis points to about 119.3 basis points a year, their highest intraday level since active trading began about a year ago, according to ICE Data Services. The spread on its 5.25% bonds due in 2036 widened 7 basis points to 121 basis points over Treasuries. Protection costs also rose for Oracle, Microsoft and Broadcom.

The new pressure followed disclosure of about $825 billion of future leases and contractual commitments, many related to computing power and AI infrastructure, compared with almost $700 billion reported in July. Quarterly free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion, against a $784 million inflow in Q2 and a $10.625 billion inflow in the third quarter of last year. Those figures gave creditors a more demanding cash-flow comparison alongside the increase in prospective obligations.

Meta had raised the bottom of its annual capital-spending range to $135 billion from $130 billion, keeping the upper end at $145 billion. That spending revision was already known; Thursday's credit response placed it beside the larger contractual commitment and the cash outflow. The company did not give capital-expenditure guidance for next year. Investors widely anticipated another bond offering after earnings and before the next Fed meeting and November 3 election, increasing the attention paid to existing spreads.

Vadim Solovey, chief executive of cloud-optimization company DoiT International, highlighted the length of Meta's commitments, including data-center leases running 18 to 30 years. He considered such agreements expensive at a time of scarce capacity, but argued that Meta was better placed than many other buyers because its established business also uses the computing resources. The distinction matters for a borrower committing cash far into the future while seeking an operating return from AI today.

Morgan Stanley's Vishwanath Tirupattur said another 100-basis-point increase in borrowing costs would be unlikely to deter hyperscaler capital expenditure. He expected the effect to be uneven, with weaker borrowers lower in the ecosystem more vulnerable. Much of the year's spread widening, in his assessment, reflected the market absorbing a large volume of new issues. A slowdown in capital spending that reduced debt supply could therefore receive a favorable reception in credit even if it weakened the expansion narrative in equities.

The disagreement over demand remained substantial. Blackstone President Jon Gray argued that AI infrastructure was being built to keep pace with existing demand, pushing back against bubble concerns voiced by Ken Griffin days earlier. BlackRock's Wei Li emphasized investors' increasing insistence on monetization as higher yields raised the hurdle for long-duration growth. Tesla's decision to reduce spending plans and weaker-than-expected guidance from chip-equipment maker Lam Research added different operating signals to Meta's confidence in its own investment returns.

China's market supplied a further deterioration in risk appetite. The CSI 300 closed 1.8% lower, bringing its decline from the June high to 20%. Chinese onshore shares had lost $2.4 trillion of market value from their recent peak, while the Hang Seng Tech Index fell about 5% Thursday. Weak consumption and doubts about AI profitability combined with disappointment over the absence of a broad spending package. Turnover in nine exchange-traded funds associated with state-backed buying reached 52 billion yuan by 2:45 p.m. local time, close to the 62.8 billion yuan seen on October 15, as authorities sought to cushion the selling.

New financing remained possible despite those losses. DeepSeek raised about $15 billion in a funding round that included CATL and Tencent among its biggest investors, according to people familiar with the transaction. Huawei secured a $2.25 billion loan from Chinese banks, according to a person familiar with that financing. These were substantial additions of capital even as public-market investors questioned valuations and future returns.

Physical constraints added another dimension to the Australian buildout. Of more than 40 large data-center projects planned or being built around Sydney and Melbourne, only 23% had publicly confirmed power supply or grid connections, Bloomberg reported. Australia had more than 20 gigawatts of announced and early-stage projects against about 1.5 gigawatts operating. Data centers already consumed roughly 2% of grid electricity, a share expected to reach 13% by 2036. Goodman had scrapped a A$1.2 billion Sydney project following hundreds of objections.

Those figures sharpen the distinction between financing announced capacity and financing capacity that can actually earn revenue. Power connections and local approvals determine when buildings become usable, while borrowing and construction commitments can precede that date. The financing debate was becoming more selective even within an industry still attracting large sums of new capital.

Thursday's broader credit performance reflected both the government-bond rally and increased risk premiums. U.S. high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. LQD, the investment-grade bond ETF, returned about 1.03%, compared with 0.18% for high-yield fund HYG and 0.45% for emerging-market bond fund EMB. Falling Treasury yields supported positive bond returns while the credit terms confronting more vulnerable borrowers deteriorated.

## France's Selloff Diverges From Core Europe

French debt suffered another pronounced deterioration as investors sold sovereign risk that they were willing to hold in the United States and Germany. The 10-year premium over Bunds widened as much as 19 basis points to 178 basis points, the largest gap since late 2011. French 10-year yields climbed as much as 13 basis points to 5.14%, their highest since 2002, before paring the rise to about 6 basis points during the reported trading period.

The selling extended to short maturities. Two-year yields rose 11 basis points to 3.86%, and the CAC 40 lost more than 1%. By contrast, Bloomberg's late U.S. market account put Germany's 10-year yield 9 basis points lower at 3.33% and Britain's 5 basis points lower at 5.33%. France's worsening premium was therefore reinforced by demand for other government bonds, not simply a common rise in European yields.

Mediolanum International Funds' Daniel Loughney reported another round of carry-position liquidations, amplified by poor liquidity. The positions had sought to earn the difference between short-dated French bonds and interest-rate swaps. Their unwinding put additional selling pressure on a market already strained by uncertainty over the government's ability to repair public finances amid cost-of-living protests.

President Emmanuel Macron said the government would aim to allow only labor-union marches on Saturday. Police banned demonstrations in parts of Paris, including near the presidential palace and along the Champs-Elysees, while other cities imposed restrictions. The prospect of renewed weekend unrest left investors assessing both fiscal negotiations and the state's capacity to contain disruption.

Aegon Investment Management's Irina Kurochkina attributed the weak sentiment to energy prices, thin liquidity and budget uncertainty. She argued that the ECB could support bonds by recognizing the yield increase as an abrupt tightening of financial conditions, reducing the urgency for further policy increases. Allspring's Henrietta Pacquement saw few near-term catalysts for restoring confidence, with next year's presidential election complicating the attraction of yields around 5%.

ECB Governing Council member Fabio Panetta supplied a distinct assessment of the economic restraint. Speaking Wednesday in Turin, he said rising yields would weigh on Europe's economy without yet constituting a crisis. The increase had been led by the United States, where stronger growth accompanied higher rates, whereas Europe was absorbing tighter financing with less robust activity. He also warned that French sovereign tensions could affect Italy's borrowing costs.

Guinness Global Investors' Craig Veysey emphasized stronger European safety nets and the absence of the banking stress that marked the earlier debt crisis. His concern was that a broader deterioration could eventually reach Germany if investors began anticipating more borrowing to support indebted neighbors. That was a prospective fiscal-sharing risk; Thursday's observed German move was a rally.

European policymakers also reached a provisional political agreement to reform securitization rules, offering a separate route to expand credit capacity. The framework would materially lower bank capital requirements for low-risk transactions while retaining higher requirements for riskier positions. It still requires finalization and formal endorsement.

The compromise introduces a new resilient category alongside the existing simple, transparent and standardized label, EU-level supervision of independent STS verifiers, and reduced administrative requirements. It would raise investment limits for UCITS funds and permit greater insurer and reinsurer participation in synthetic securitizations, including transactions financing projects before they become operational. Europe's outstanding securitizations, including collateralized loan obligations, totaled EUR1.295 trillion at the end of March, up 6.3% in a year, according to the Association for Financial Markets in Europe.

The proposed changes seek to free bank capital for household, corporate and infrastructure lending, including defense and climate-resilience investment. They address the capacity and cost of credit intermediation while France's selloff demonstrates how quickly sovereign funding conditions can tighten. The reform's benefits depend on completing the framework and attracting investor participation under the revised rules.

## Policy Decisions Expose Different Inflation Constraints

The Philippines delivered the day's clearest tightening surprise, raising its target reverse-repurchase rate 50 basis points to 5.50%. Only one of 25 economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected that size of increase; the other 24 anticipated 25 basis points. Governor Eli Remolona described urgency in responding to a worse-than-expected inflation outlook, with the central bank signaling readiness to act again.

The BSP maintained its 2026 inflation forecast at 6.1% but raised the 2027 projection to 6% from 5.4%, with inflation expected to moderate to 3.3% only in 2028. September inflation had accelerated to 7.2%, reversing four months of deceleration and taking the year-to-date average to 5.4%, above the 3% target. Higher oil prices, increased transport fares and the risk of a severe El Nino drought complicated the outlook for an economy growing at its slowest pace since the pandemic.

The peso reached another record low despite the increase. Remolona acknowledged the imported-inflation pressure but said reserves would not be depleted to defend a particular exchange rate. The cumulative tightening since the Iran war began reached 125 basis points. Pantheon Macroeconomics' Miguel Chanco considered the possibility that the larger move front-loaded an increase otherwise likely in December, rather than guaranteeing another rise then.

South Korea unanimously held its seven-day repo rate at 3%, as all 24 surveyed economists expected, after quarter-point increases in July and August. The pause came with a stronger growth assessment: the Bank of Korea said this year and next would considerably exceed its August forecasts of 3.3% and 2.9%. Governor Shin Hyun Song said the earlier increases had created room to assess domestic conditions without reacting mechanically to short-term market movements.

The bank also expected next year's core inflation to be slightly higher than the previously projected 2.5%, with updated forecasts due in November. Its earlier headline forecasts were 2.7% for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027. Shin allowed for inflation to approach target more gradually rather than requiring an immediate return next year. State Street's Jiuk Choi expected at least one additional increase followed by an extended hold while core inflation slowed toward the low-to-mid 2% range by the end of 2027.

The domestic detail explained the cautious pacing. Working-day-adjusted exports rose 65.9% in the first 20 days of October from a year earlier, and chip exports surged 222.5%. Yet household bank lending increased only 600 billion won in September, its smallest rise since March, as mortgage growth slowed. Seoul apartment prices still increased 0.13% in the week through October 19, extending their run to 89 weeks. Three-year government yields rose as much as 3 basis points earlier Thursday, and the won strengthened as much as 0.3% to 1,322.75 per dollar.

Turkey moved toward easing instead. Its central bank lowered the one-week repo rate to 36% from 37%, the first cut since the Iran war began, and reduced overnight lending and borrowing rates to 39% and 34.5%. September annual inflation had slowed to 29.7%, its lowest since November 2021, while demand and economic activity also moderated. Governor Fatih Karahan's committee retained a meeting-by-meeting approach focused on the inflation outlook.

The decision also followed severe stress in domestic investment funds. Regulators ordered 131 funds worth about $20 billion into liquidation. Of nearly half a million affected investors, fewer than 50,000 had received payments totaling 40.8 billion liras, Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said this week. The central bank had increased repo funding and eased some small-business credit-growth limits to relieve liquidity strains. Is Asset Management's Hande Sekerci expected the negative wealth effect to weaken consumption and create room for further easing, while acknowledging the bank's caution about October inflation fluctuations.

Mexico's fresh inflation release made its own policy choice more difficult. Annual consumer-price growth accelerated to 3.62% in the first half of October, above the 3.59% consensus and 3.49% in late September. Core inflation rose to 3.78%, exceeding the 3.70% forecast and the prior 3.71%. Banxico has held its benchmark at 6.5% since June and recently replaced guidance favoring continued holds with a more data-dependent approach. The new readings raised pressure before its November 5 decision, even as the bank continued to project convergence to its 3% target in Q4 2027.

Czech Deputy Governor Jan Frait offered a more guarded response to energy inflation. Arguments for another increase on November 5 were relatively strong, he said, but market rates were already restraining activity. Three-year swaps, important for mortgage pricing, had risen about 150 basis points since the Iran war began to near 4.9%. Core inflation was 3.1%, while new mortgage activity was showing early signs of moderation and corporate credit remained robust.

Frait rejected the need for 100 basis points of increases over the next year under current conditions, questioning whether market pricing partly reflected liquidity or mechanical models. Even 50 basis points would look abrupt to him if the economy remained resilient and global inflation pressure persisted. He would respond if lending failed to slow, demand remained strong and wage claims increased. His distinction was between responding to persistent domestic pressure and adding to a tightening already delivered by longer market rates.

Japan's long end attracted a different kind of response. BNP Paribas Asset Management's James McAlevey said the firm had increased 20- and 30-year JGB exposure from a very small position early in the year to moderate or medium size. Some flexible strategies paired it with shorts in two- and five-year debt. He cited the steep curve, dollar-hedged yields around 6%-6.5%, and renewed domestic demand; Japanese insurers had been net buyers of super-long bonds for four months. Further confidence would depend on constrained fiscal action and continued, roughly quarterly BOJ normalization, with a stronger yen helping restrain imported inflation.

## Financing Continues as Individual Credits Deteriorate

JetBlue's securities suffered a fresh collapse ahead of next week's earnings. Its $2 billion of loyalty-program-backed bonds due in 2031 fell to about 40 cents on the dollar, a record low, from around 80 cents at the start of October. Shares dropped nearly 10% to $2.65, their lowest since the airline went public in 2002. High fuel costs confronted an already heavily indebted carrier with years of losses and a price-sensitive leisure customer base.

The company reiterated confidence in its turnaround and its target of at least $1 a share in earnings in 2028. It had previously projected positive free cash flow in 2027 and reported more than $6 billion of unencumbered assets. Second-quarter free cash flow was negative $389 million, including $155 million consumed by operations and $234 million of capital expenditure. Its average fuel cost of $4.23 a gallon was 76% above a year earlier. Moody's Caa2 rating and forecast of losses this year and next framed the company's effort to reassure creditors.

Turkish power company Zorlu Enerji was preparing to seek a delay of up to six months on roughly $55 million of interest due Friday on its $1.1 billion bond, according to people familiar with the matter. The 2030 notes were indicated in the mid-50s Thursday. Fitch had downgraded the company to B- on negative watch in September, citing weakening liquidity and reliance on short-term refinancing. It reported $124.5 million maturing within 12 months as of June, expected negative free cash flow in 2026 and 2027, and forecast interest costs consuming about 65% of cash EBITDA this year.

EyeCare Partners was approaching a conditional creditor agreement that would reduce debt through asset sales. Lenders including Anchorage Capital, Diameter and King Street would accept discounts if businesses were sold within an agreed period; slower sales would reduce the discount, and failure to sell would eliminate it. The best-case reduction was $300 million-$400 million out of roughly $2 billion of debt, according to a person familiar with the terms.

The optometry sale to MyEyeDr, expected to close in Q4 subject to regulatory approvals, would fund repayment at par of a $110 million first-out revolver and $286 million first-out term loan. About $164 million of first-lien second-out debt would be repaid at a 12-cent discount to par, S&P said. A distressed exchange would move participating second-out lenders into a new first-lien 1.5-out loan, with options to extend payment-in-kind interest beyond early 2027 and maturity beyond November 2028. The ranking and timing of claims, not just the headline debt reduction, determine the bargain for different creditors.

Other transactions demonstrated continuing access to private financing. Blackstone led a $300 million package for Arlington Capital Partners' take-private of aerospace and defense components maker Gooch & Housego, after Arlington initially funded the acquisition with equity. The financing comprised a unitranche loan, delayed-draw term loan and revolver, with JPMorgan and Jefferies also participating.

Texas developer KDC was seeking about $3.5 billion to build AT&T's new Plano headquarters through credit-tenant-lease financing, according to people familiar with the plans. CGA Capital and CBRE were arranging debt with an expected weighted-average life of 18.7 years. The structure relies on rent from the investment-grade tenant rather than the underlying property, and the proposed scale far exceeds the $25 million-$100 million range typical of such transactions cited by PGIM.

Blackstone's own earnings illustrated the uneven operating environment. Distributable earnings fell 9.2% to $1.72 billion, or $1.32 a share, exceeding the $1.26 consensus, as deal activity slowed. Credit and insurance earnings rose 4% to $433 million and the business accounted for more than half of $63.3 billion of quarterly inflows. Infrastructure returned 6.4%, supported in part by data-center leasing, while real-estate and private-equity distributable earnings declined 10% and 7%. Deployment of $30.1 billion was the year's quarterly low, despite $228.9 billion of available capital.

Sovereign borrowers were also seeking alternative funding. Indonesia met investors in Shanghai for a potential 7 billion-10 billion yuan panda sale planned for November through early December, potentially spanning three, five and seven years. It has approval for up to 30 billion yuan through 2028. Financing official Suminto cited relatively low costs and a broader investor base as reasons for returning after July's 7 billion yuan debut, while MSCI-related outflow risks continued to complicate its financial backdrop.

South Africa's Treasury identified a different funding vulnerability beneath the national budget: municipal debt to creditors had risen 19% to 185.2 billion rand in the year through June. Overdue municipal obligations to Eskom alone reached 122.5 billion rand by August 31. Treasury warned that distressed public entities could require more national funding or guarantees, after Eskom had already received 220 billion rand of a 230 billion rand relief package. Proposed municipal-finance reforms would impose personal liability for irregular spending, permit Treasury appointment of municipal chief financial officers and require councils to account for unfunded budgets.

Nigeria's Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele expected the federal deficit to undershoot its 4.2%-of-GDP target as revenues improved and borrowing costs declined. The World Bank's broader consolidated forecast pointed toward a widening deficit including state and local governments. The ministry also disputed a comparison showing first-half interest payments exceeding federal revenue by 24%, saying the interest measure included obligations serviced for other tiers while the revenue measure omitted receipts. The competing fiscal perimeters are central to judging that burden, with total public debt up 21% year on year to $121 billion in June.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's October flash S&P Global PMIs arrive after a rally that has moved beyond the long end and reduced expectations of near-term Fed tightening. Manufacturing consensus is 55.5 against 55.9 previously, and services 58 against 58.8, with publication at 13:45 UTC. The composite's calendar forecast is 57.6 after 58.4. Their activity readings will provide a broader comparison with Thursday's low initial claims and softer regional manufacturing figures, when investors are increasingly sensitive to the growth cost of expensive capital.

Final October Michigan figures follow at 14:00 UTC. Sentiment is expected at 46.3 after 48.1, current conditions at 44.7 after 50.9, and inflation expectations at 4.7% over one year and 3.5% over five years, versus 4.6% and 3.4%. Weakening confidence with persistent expected inflation would leave the Fed facing a different mix from a slowdown accompanied by falling price expectations. Thursday's sharp real-yield decline has made that distinction more consequential for the durability of the rally.

Monday brings the September Chicago Fed National Activity Index, with a calendar forecast of -0.1 after -0.04, October Dallas Fed manufacturing, forecast at 7 after 9.8, and a two-year Treasury auction. The activity data extend the breadth of the growth assessment; the auction will put actual financing demand beside the large repricing in short Treasury yields.

AI funding remains an immediate corporate test. Meta's larger commitments and cash outflow leave the terms and size of any new borrowing important, while next week's Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon earnings will provide separate updates on spending and revenue conversion. JetBlue's earnings arrive with its secured bonds near 40 cents, making liquidity and cash generation particularly pressing. Zorlu Enerji's Friday coupon deadline will determine the next step in its proposed payment deferral.

France's weekend demonstrations and the government's response retain direct significance after the spread shock and carry liquidations. Whether liquidity improves matters alongside fiscal progress: forced selling has already reached short maturities. The separate energy risk remains active as attacks threaten Saudi infrastructure even where operations continue. Another rise in fuel costs could intensify the pressure on both household demand and inflation, while the Philippines' forecast revision shows how persistently that combination can constrain monetary policy.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries surge as technology losses and French debt stress deepen growth concerns
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied across maturities as a global technology selloff and French sovereign stress prompted demand for safety and a reassessment of growth. The 10-year yield fell 16.6 basis points to 4.953%, below 5% for the first time in about a month; the 2-year fell 16.64 basis points to 4.6396%. Traders shifted the next fully priced Fed increase from December to January, while Treasury futures short covering amplified the advance. A 13.77-basis-point decline in the 10-year real yield accounted for most of the move, alongside a smaller 2.83-basis-point fall in breakeven inflation.

Meta's roughly $825 billion of future leases and contractual commitments and $2.12 billion quarterly free-cash-flow deficit sharpened concerns about AI investment returns. Its default-protection costs reached an intraday record, while U.S. high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. France diverged from the rally in core government debt: its premium over Germany reached 178 basis points during trading as fiscal uncertainty, thin liquidity and carry-position liquidations drove selling into short maturities.

Oil continued rising amid attacks on Saudi infrastructure, leaving expensive energy a threat to both spending and inflation. The Philippines surprised with a 50-basis-point increase, South Korea held rates while strengthening its growth assessment, and Turkey cut as inflation slowed. Friday's U.S. activity and inflation-expectations releases will help distinguish a growth slowdown from a more difficult combination of weaker demand and persistent price pressure.
